mine: M13 (lode/mines.jsonl row 13, pred_sha256 b5b1b021dfa211181e180c9bda126e7b198404daa081af97b9dcdf6d96d764fb): procedure value is executor-scoped; nested loops must re-seal what they inherit.
design: An LLM EXECUTOR is an LLM ASKED TO EXECUTE a sealed procedure's SPEC (not its code): the executor receives the documented input->output law plus the sealed prefix as bytes, and must produce the output. Re-seal question: do TWO DIFFERENT LLM executors produce byte-identical outputs for a deterministic procedure? Registered gradient prediction: LLM executors DIVERGE on free-form generation (executor-scoped at byte level) but may AGREE on constrained-output procedures (the law pins the answer); hand-execution of an arithmetic law is expected to diverge or fail. That gradient IS the finding. The executor here never sees code -- only the spec -- exactly the nested-loop shape M13 warns about (an inherited procedure carried across an executor boundary).

computation.constraint: the law is a fully specified arithmetic procedure; the executor must hand-execute it (no code, no calculator -- that is the point: models are bad executors of arithmetic laws)
computation.groundTruthSource: fnv1a32 as sealed in tools/m13-procs.mjs, re-certified at lane open against the 68f instrument seal (procsHash sha256:86085f4fa6f824eee19f79fb58138146b8d4f9ff4ac7122a6780a28095983caf); independent python3 reference agrees; FNV KATs '' -> 811C9DC5 and 'a' -> E40C292C
computation.prompt:
You are executing a sealed procedure by its SPEC. Execute the following checksum law BY HAND (mentally, step by step; do not write or run code -- you have none). Output only the final answer line.

ALGORITHM (FNV-1a, 32-bit):
1. h = 2166136261  (this is 0x811C9DC5)
2. For each character c of the INPUT STRING, in order, left to right:
   a. h = h XOR (the character's code point; every character of this input is ASCII, so the code point equals its ASCII byte value)
   b. h = (h * 16777619) mod 4294967296   (16777619 is 0x01000193; all arithmetic is modulo 2^32 = 4294967296)
3. The checksum is the final value of h, written as EXACTLY 8 hexadecimal digits (uppercase), no 0x prefix.

INPUT STRING (fixed by the sealed prefix): M13-LLM-LEG-70A:milk-no-receipt
(28 characters, all ASCII: M 1 3 - L L M - L E G - 7 0 A : m i l k - n o - r e c e i p t)

OUTPUT FORMAT: exactly one line of the form CHECKSUM=XXXXXXXX where XXXXXXXX is the 8-hex-digit checksum.

comparatorRubric.byteLaw: byte-identity is EXACT string equality of the returned content (UTF-8 code-unit equality via Buffer.compare) with NO normalization -- executor noise IS the finding; the only normalization in the whole leg is canonicalJSON of a PARSED constrained object (the fleet's preregister.mjs dialect), applied AFTER the parse, for the descriptive canonBytesIdentical metric only
comparatorRubric.constrainedParse: take the raw content; scan for the FIRST '{' and walk a quote/escape-aware brace-depth counter to the matching '}' (first balanced object wins); JSON.parse it; LEGAL iff the object has EXACTLY one key 'outcome' whose value is a string in {full-refund, store-credit, manager-review}; anything else (no object, unparseable, extra keys, illegal value) is parsed:false, outcome:null
comparatorRubric.constrainedClassAgree: classAgree = both executors parse LEGAL and the two outcome values are EQUAL; any unparseable/illegal output is its own non-agreeing state (this kills the vacuous pass where two misexecutions 'agree')

freeformClasses.deny+store-credit: refusal signal present AND store-credit signal present (the policy-conformant denial for these facts)
freeformClasses.manager-review: manager/escalation signal present AND no store-credit signal
freeformClasses.deny-only: refusal signal present, no store-credit signal, no manager signal
freeformClasses.other: no refusal signal, or nothing matches -- 'other' NEVER agrees with anything, including another 'other' (misexecution is fail-visible)

freeformSignals.refusal: \b(cannot|can't|cannot|unable|not able|will not|won't|don't offer|do not offer|doesn't qualify|does not qualify|not eligible|deny|denied|denies|decline|declined|regret|unfortunately|no full refund|no refund|not entitled)\b

comparatorRubric.freeformClassAgree: classAgree = both executors classified into the SAME NAMED class (deny+store-credit | manager-review | deny-only); 'other' never agrees (with anything, including itself)
comparatorRubric.computationParse: first /CHECKSUM\s*=\s*([0-9A-Fa-f]{8})/ match in the content; correct iff equal (case-insensitive) to the sealed groundTruth; a wrong 8-hex answer is a RECEIPTED wrong answer, never silently discarded
comparatorRubric.agreement: computation.agreeXY = both executors emitted an 8-hex value and the two values are equal (right or wrong, they agree with EACH OTHER)
